reaction: That distinction makes the argument more precise.

reaction: The distinction between pleasure and endless indulgence is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Epicurus's argument against fearing death was most worthwhile: its premises and the distinction between being dead and painful dying made the reasoning clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final combination felt somewhat predictable after the argument against fear; it added a broader picture of pleasure but required no meaningful choice.

surprise.text: The distinction between voluntarily needing less and forced poverty sharpened the Diogenes example.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the last two were the only offered combinations rather than choices between alternatives.

continue.text: I would continue: the contrasting schools and their carefully qualified arguments made me curious about how later thinkers respond.
